newsitem.title: UK: Euro fuel barges dip, low sulphur paper holds up.
newsitem.headline: Euro fuel barges dip, low sulphur paper holds up.

text.p: European fuel oil barge prices were softer on poor bunker demand on Wednesday while solid swaps were holding up low sulphur fuel values, traders said.
High sulphur barges traded at $83.25 and $83.50 fob a tonne in Antwerp while very prompt Rotterdam material was offered at $82.50.
Material was offered for dates further out at around $84/$85. Dealers said poor bunker demand was pulling the prompt market down.
Low sulphur swaps were firm at $96.50/$97.50 for June, with New York harbour numbers still seen as supportive.
But physical business was quiet, with Friday's deal seen as having stymied the market.

"Near-term barrels are not being shown. It has all gone quiet since the last deal, which rather surprised the market," one trader said. "Physical is definetly under June swaps at the moment but its unclear by how much."

Low sulphur straight-run markets were checked by a deal at $108 a tonne fob on Tuesday from a U.S. refiner who off-loaded barrels to a French major, which was considered by some as below current rates.
Other sellers were offering at above $110 fob a tonne.
"The deal has taken one cheap cargo out and we're waiting now for a serious bid," said one producer.
